Ratio1+D, D=AB-1=(1/2)E_(e,f)[(r_e-r_f)²/(r_e r_f)] measures dispersion, not common calibration: r=rho gives zero gap. Positive target coefficients on p=0 edges need no relative envelope/query for these witnesses, but may affect the true response under mismatch. No arbitrary high-contrast solution follows from their zero reference work.

Partition EDGES into disjoint cells sharing boundary vertices; include terminals and vertices incident to other cells in each boundary. E_K0=sum_K c0(dh0)²; reference injection b_K=H_K f0_K vanishes in cell interiors. Acquire target coefficients and solve D_K=min_(h|boundary=h0)sum_K c(dh)², N_K=min_(H_K f=b_K)sum_K f²/c. Boundary-compatible potentials glue; same injection flows sum to globally conserved reference flux. Thus C0²/sum N_K<=C<=sum D_K. Fixed boundary work <dh,f>=E_K0 yields D_K N_K>=(E_K0)². For positive-work cells w=E_K0/C0,u=D_K/E_K0,v=N_K/E_K0, uv>=1 and C0/E_w v<=C<=C0 E_w u. Zero-work cells have zero energies for positive targets. Coarsening reduces both summed energies, tightening both ends; a WHOLE-network cell becomes exact only by acquiring/solving the full target. Monotonicity is not affordability.

Given justified0<a<=r<=b on positive-reference-work support, R=b/a, a<=u<=b and1/b<=v<=1/a. Set A=E_wu,B=E_wv,Delta=AB-1. Source proves Var(u)/A²<=R Delta and Var(v)/B²<=R Delta from E[(X-EX)²/X]=EX(EX E1/X-1) and uv>=1. No spatial independence/stationarity required for fixed coefficients. Delta=chi²(w||q)+A E_w(v-1/u), q=wu/A, separates between-cell redistribution from within-cell potential/flux incompatibility. More samples do not erase either intrinsic error.

This counts CELLS, not coefficients. Whole cost includes graph/reference/weights/sampling/statistics and every distinct cell's coefficients, TWO solves and precision; expected acquisition sum_K[1-(1-w_K)^n]T_K.
